# Harness Execution Summary

The candidate harness fails catastrophically on ds_alpha and ds_gamma (0% accuracy) and barely recovers on ds_beta (37.5%), revealing systemic design flaws. Two distinct failure modes emerge: on ds_alpha/gamma, predictions are individual words extracted directly from inputs rather than the required hyphenated compound labels; on ds_beta (multiple-choice), the model exhibits severe default-to-first-option bias, repeatedly predicting the same answer regardless of input variations. The memory mechanism is entirely inactive—memory state remains empty throughout all runs and never accumulates knowledge from training steps, indicating the learning loop doesn't actually encode information. The fixed 191-char context persists but appears unused; online learning with single-example batches fails to improve generalization from step zero. To recover, redesign memory persistence, enforce output constraints against valid option sets, and validate that learned patterns actually influence predictions during evaluation.
